title: Why do we procrastinate?
reason: 上一课关注无人驾驶汽车与人机交互，今天轮换到生产力与项目管理。本集从截止时间、工作压力和情绪反应解释拖延，并讨论任务拆分等应对方法，适合迁移到项目交付、学习计划和工程管理场景。练习通过重复调用常见动词搭配和工作表达，帮助把被动理解转化为主动输出。

targetExpressions.meaning: begin doing something, especially a task that needs effort
targetExpressions.usage: Use it when encouraging action: The task is large, but we can make a start with the first section.

targetExpressions.meaning: finish required work by the agreed time
targetExpressions.usage: Use it for time-bound work: We reduced the scope so the team could meet the deadline.

targetExpressions.expression: put something off until the last minute
targetExpressions.meaning: delay something until very little time remains
targetExpressions.usage: Use it for avoidable delay: I put the report off until the last minute and had to rush.

targetExpressions.expression: without a shadow of a doubt
targetExpressions.usage: Use it to strongly emphasise certainty: Without a shadow of a doubt, clear priorities helped the project.

targetExpressions.meaning: feeling stressed or anxious because there is too much to do
targetExpressions.usage: Use it for a demanding situation: People may make quick decisions when they are under pressure.

targetExpressions.expression: break down the task into smaller stages
targetExpressions.meaning: divide a large piece of work into smaller, manageable steps
targetExpressions.usage: Use it to describe practical planning: We broke down the task into smaller stages and assigned an owner to each one.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete Sam's encouragement to Neil: “Come on, Neil, let's ______!”
objectiveQuestions.explanation: At the start of the transcript, Sam says, “Come on, Neil, let's make a start!” because she has unfinished work.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What does it mean to “put something off until the last minute”?
objectiveQuestions.targetExpression: put something off until the last minute

options.text: Delay it until very little time remains.
Finish it well before it is required.
Give the whole task to another person.
Remove the deadline from the task.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Neil says Sam delayed repeatedly and put her work off until the last minute; the programme defines procrastination as delaying necessary work until later.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete Eshaan's explanation: “I've told myself that I procrastinate because I work better ______.”
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Eshaan says he has told himself that he works better under pressure, meaning while feeling stressed or anxious.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: When Eshaan says he is a procrastinator “without a shadow of a doubt”, what is he communicating?
objectiveQuestions.targetExpression: without a shadow of a doubt

options.text: He is making a careful guess.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript explains that the phrase emphasises complete certainty.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the work-related collocation from the transcript: Sam has a deadline to ______ today.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Sam says, “I've got a deadline to meet today,” so the natural collocation is meet a deadline.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: According to Neil, why can it help to “break down the task into smaller stages”?
objectiveQuestions.targetExpression: break down the task into smaller stages

options.text: It can reduce how threatening the workload feels.
It removes every deadline from the work.
It guarantees that someone else will finish the task.
It creates more emotional pressure on purpose.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Neil says that breaking the task into smaller stages also breaks down the level of threat a person feels from the workload.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What percentage of people in the research procrastinated enough to interfere with day-to-day life?
objectiveQuestions.targetExpression: put something off until the last minute
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Neil reveals that around 20 percent have a procrastination habit strong enough to make life difficult.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Use the transcript expression to complete the project sentence: “We should review the migration plan now instead of ______ it ______ until the last minute.”
objectiveQuestions.targetExpression: put something off until the last minute
objectiveQuestions.explanation: After “instead of”, the natural form is putting it off; the object may be placed between put and off.

subjectiveQuestions.prompt: Write one sentence of 10–25 words. Why does Eshaan say he procrastinates? Start: “He tells himself that he…” and use “under pressure”.
subjectiveQuestions.gradingCriteria: A supported answer should say that Eshaan tells himself he works better under pressure. First judge whether the response answers the question, then check whether the requested target expression is used naturally. Point out only one or two high-value improvements. Do not penalise simple but correct English for not being advanced. If needed, suggest only one alternative from today's target expressions or transcript. assessment.retellingPrompt: Without looking at the full transcript, retell the episode in 80–120 words using this structure: (1) problem—what procrastination is and its possible effects; (2) explanation—pressure, emotions and impulsive behaviour; (3) response—one practical way to begin. Phrase bank: “put something off until the last minute”, “under pressure”, “break down the task into smaller stages”. Use at least two phrases naturally. Simple, accurate sentences are enough.
referencePoints: Procrastination means delaying necessary work, often because it is difficult, boring or unpleasant.
The programme links procrastination with higher stress, lower wellbeing and lower financial or career success.
Eshaan says he tells himself that he works better under pressure and may get emotional gratification from last-minute work.
The programme presents procrastination as an emotional response connected with impulsive behaviour, not only poor time management.
Breaking a task into smaller stages can reduce how threatening the workload feels.
Forgiving past procrastination may help a person avoid repeating it in the future.
